itinerary.theme: Bazaar, temples and a hilltop sunset
itinerary.summary: Ease in around Hampi Bazaar, the living Virupaksha Temple and the boulder-strewn Hemakuta Hill.

place.name: Virupaksha Temple
place.description: Still in worship after 1,300 years, its 50-metre gopuram anchors the old bazaar. Inside, Lakshmi the temple elephant blesses visitors most mornings, and a pinhole in one hall projects an inverted image of the tower.

morning.tip: Shoulders and knees covered, shoes left at the gate; arrive before 9:30 to see the morning puja.

place.name: Hampi Bazaar and the Kadalekalu Ganesha
place.description: Walk the kilometre-long colonnade where traders once sold gems by the heap, then climb to the giant monolithic Ganesha and the smaller Sasivekalu Ganesha on the hill's flank. Lunch on a banana-leaf thali at one of the bazaar's family kitchens.

afternoon.tip: Midday is hot on the rocks; carry at least a litre of water each.

place.name: Hemakuta Hill sunset
place.description: A low granite hill scattered with early temples, where the whole valley turns gold at dusk. It's an easy ten-minute climb from the bazaar and the best first view of Hampi.

evening.tip: Sit facing west on the slabs behind the twin-tower temples; leave before full dark, the path has no lights.

itinerary.theme: Vittala's stone chariot and the river
itinerary.summary: The grandest temple complex in Hampi, then a coracle out on the Tungabhadra.

place.name: Vittala Temple and Stone Chariot
place.description: The finest carving in Hampi: musical pillars that ring when tapped (now roped off), and the stone chariot pictured on India's ₹50 note. Early light is softest and crowds are thin.

morning.tip: The combined ASI ticket also covers Lotus Mahal and the Elephant Stables, so keep it for tomorrow.

place.name: Coracle ride on the Tungabhadra
place.description: Spin downriver in a bamboo-and-tarp basket boat past riverside shrines and carvings you can't reach on foot. Boatmen gather near the Kodandarama ghat and the path from Vittala.

afternoon.tip: Agree the price and route before you step in; life jackets are usually on board, ask for them.

place.name: Malyavanta Raghunatha Temple at dusk
place.description: A hilltop temple to Rama, far quieter than Matanga, with carved fish and sea creatures on the boulders and a wide sunset view east of the ruins.

evening.tip: Have your auto driver wait; return autos are scarce after dark.

itinerary.dayTip: Hire one auto-rickshaw for the day (around ₹1,000-1,500); distances between sites are bigger than they look.

itinerary.summary: Palaces, the queen's bath and a last sunset by a lake.

place.name: Lotus Mahal and Elephant Stables
place.description: An Indo-Islamic pavilion of arches and lotus-bud domes inside the walled women's quarter, next to the eleven domed stables built for the royal elephants.

morning.tip: Same ticket as Vittala Temple yesterday.

place.name: Hazara Rama Temple and Queen's Bath
place.description: The palace chapel's walls are a stone comic strip of the Ramayana and royal processions. Ten minutes away, the Queen's Bath is a plain-fronted building hiding a carved arcaded pool.

afternoon.tip: Lunch at a Kamalapura dhaba on the way; it's the closest village to the royal centre.

place.name: Sanapur Lake
place.description: Across the river, a reservoir ringed by boulders where locals swim and couples watch the sun drop behind the rocks. A calm, green contrast to the ruins.

evening.tip: Swimming isn't safe in all seasons; enjoy it from the rocks unless locals confirm it's calm.

stays.name: Heritage Resort Hampi
stays.why: Cottages with gardens a short drive from the royal centre; quiet for couples.

stays.name: Evolve Back Kamalapura Palace
stays.why: A palace-style splurge with a pool and guided heritage walks for a special occasion.

stays.name: Anegundi homestays
stays.why: Simple village rooms across the river, close to Sanapur Lake and Anjanadri Hill.

essentials.currency: Indian Rupee (INR). UPI and cards work in towns; carry cash for small temples, coracles and rural stalls.
essentials.language: Kannada; Hindi and English understood in Hampi
essentials.tipping: Not expected; round up for guides and drivers
essentials.weather: Oct-Feb is dry and warm (15-30°C). Mar-May is very hot; Jun-Sep brings monsoon green but some closures.
essentials.gettingAround: Hosapete is the nearest railhead (13 km). Autos and rented bicycles or scooters cover the sites.

packing: Light cotton clothes that cover knees and shoulders
Small torch for sunset walks back

summary.overview: Three unhurried days among the boulder fields and temple ruins of the Vijayanagara capital, timed so you catch the soft light at sunrise and sunset, with a coracle ride on the Tungabhadra and quiet dinners for two.
highlights: Sunset over the ruins from Hemakuta Hill
The stone chariot at Vittala Temple
A round coracle ride on the Tungabhadra
Lotus Mahal and the royal Elephant Stables
